title: Sifatlar: odam va narsalarni tasvirlash
goal_uz: Dars oxirida odamning tashqi ko‘rinishi va xarakterini kamida sakkizta gap bilan tasvirlaysiz, sifatlarni to‘g‘ri o‘rinda ishlatasiz, very, quite va too ni farqlaysiz hamda o‘ndan ortiq qarama-qarshi sifat juftini bilasiz.

scenes.title: Sifatlar darsiga xush kelibsiz
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda “can” va “can’t” yordamida nima qila olishimiz va nima qila olmasligimizni aytishni o‘rgandik. Bugun esa odamlarni va narsalarni tasvirlaymiz: tashqi ko‘rinish, xarakter, o‘lcham va rang. “Very”, “quite” va “too” so‘zlarini, sifatlarning qarama-qarshi juftlarini ham o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Hello! Today we will describe people and things. My friend Anna is tall and slim. She is very kind.
scenes.say_uz: Salom! Bugun odamlar va narsalarni tasvirlaymiz. Do‘stim Anna baland bo‘yli va xipcha. U juda mehribon.

scenes.title: Sifat nima?
scenes.say_native: Sifat, inglizcha “adjective”, odam yoki narsa qanday ekanini bildiradi: baland, mehribon, katta, qizil, yangi. O‘zbek tilida “qanday?” savoliga javob beradigan so‘zlar. Ingliz tilida sifat ko‘pincha “be” fe’li bilan ishlatiladi: “She is tall” — u baland bo‘yli.
scenes.say: The bag is red. My brother is funny. The room is big.
scenes.say_uz: Sumka qizil. Akam kulgili. Xona katta.

scenes.title: Bo‘y va gavda
scenes.say_native: Tashqi ko‘rinishdan boshlaymiz. Bo‘y haqida: “tall” — baland bo‘yli, “short” — past bo‘yli, “medium height” — o‘rta bo‘yli. Gavda haqida: “slim” — xipcha, chiroyli ozg‘in, bu maqtov so‘zi. “Thin” — ozg‘in, ba’zan juda ozg‘in degan ma’noda. E’tibor bering, odam uchun “high” emas, “tall” ishlatiladi.
scenes.say: He is tall and slim. She is short. My dad is medium height.
scenes.say_uz: U baland bo‘yli va xipcha. U past bo‘yli. Dadam o‘rta bo‘yli.

scenes.title: Soch va ko‘z
board: She has got long dark hair.
dark / fair / blond / grey · brown / blue / green eyes

examples.t: She has got long curly hair.

scenes.say_native: Soch va ko‘zni tasvirlash uchun “have got” yoki “has got” ishlatiladi: “She has got long dark hair” — uning uzun qora sochi bor. Uzunlik: “long”, “short”. Shakl: “straight” — tekis, “curly” — jingalak, “wavy” — to‘lqinsimon. Rang: “dark” — qora yoki to‘q, “fair” yoki “blond” — sariq, “grey” — oq oralagan, chal.
scenes.say: She has got long, curly, dark hair. He has got short, straight, fair hair and blue eyes.
scenes.say_uz: Uning uzun, jingalak, qora sochi bor. Uning kalta, tekis, sariq sochi va ko‘k ko‘zlari bor.

scenes.title: Yosh va chiroy

examples.t: My grandfather is old but very active.

scenes.say_native: Yosh haqida: “young” — yosh, “middle-aged” — o‘rta yoshli, “old” — keksa. Keksa odam haqida hurmat bilan “elderly” deyish ham mumkin. Chiroy haqida: “beautiful” va “pretty” odatda ayollar, qizlar va bolalar uchun, “handsome” esa erkaklar uchun ishlatiladi. “Good-looking” — ko‘rkam, ham erkakka, ham ayolga aytiladi.
scenes.say: She is young and very pretty. He is middle-aged and handsome. They are both good-looking.
scenes.say_uz: U yosh va juda chiroyli. U o‘rta yoshli va kelishgan. Ikkalasi ham ko‘rkam.

scenes.title: Hair — sanalmaydi
board: ✗ He is high. → ✓ He is tall.
scenes.say_native: Ikki keng tarqalgan xato. Birinchisi: “hairs”. Boshdagi sochni aytganda “hair” ko‘plik qo‘shimchasisiz ishlatiladi: “She has got long hair.” “Hairs” faqat alohida tola sochlar haqida, masalan sho‘rvada ikki dona soch topsangiz. Ikkinchisi: odam haqida “high” deyish.
scenes.say: Not: long hairs. Say: long hair. Not: He is high. Say: He is tall.
scenes.say_uz: Long hairs emas, long hair deng. He is high emas, He is tall deng.

scenes.title: Fat — qo‘pol so‘z
board: ✓ He is a bit overweight. / He is quite big.
scenes.say_native: Muhim odob qoidasi. “Fat” — semiz degan so‘z, lekin odamning yuziga yoki u haqida aytilganda qo‘pol va haqoratli eshitiladi. Muloyimroq aytish uchun “a bit overweight” — biroz ortiqcha vaznli, yoki “quite big” — ancha katta gavdali, deyiladi. Yana bir usul: “He isn’t very slim.” Xuddi shunday “old” o‘rniga ba’zan “elderly” deyish yumshoqroq.
scenes.say: He is a bit overweight. He isn't very slim. She is elderly.
scenes.say_uz: U biroz ortiqcha vaznli. U unchalik xipcha emas. U keksa yoshda.

scenes.title: Tasvirlang
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ekranda Tom haqida ma’lumot bor: bo‘yi bir metr to‘qson santimetr, vazni yetmish kilogramm, yigirma besh yoshda, sochi qisqa va qora, ko‘zlari jigarrang. Uni uch-to‘rtta gap bilan tasvirlang. “Tom is …” va “He has got …” qoliplaridan foydalaning. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Describe Tom. How tall is he? How old is he? What is his hair like?
scenes.say_uz: Tomni tasvirlang. Uning bo‘yi qanday? U necha yoshda? Sochi qanday?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: He has got short black hair and brown eyes.
scenes.say_native: Mumkin bo‘lgan javob: “Tom is tall and slim. He is young. He has got short black hair and brown eyes.” Agar siz “short, black hair” deb, ikki sifatni ketma-ket ishlatgan bo‘lsangiz, zo‘r. Avval uzunlik, keyin rang keladi: “short black hair”, “black short hair” emas. Bu tartib haqida keyinroq batafsil gaplashamiz.
scenes.say: Tom is tall and slim. He is young. He has got short black hair and brown eyes.
scenes.say_uz: Tom baland bo‘yli va xipcha. U yosh. Uning qisqa qora sochi va jigarrang ko‘zlari bor.

scenes.title: Xarakter: ijobiy sifatlar
scenes.say_native: Endi xarakter. Ijobiy sifatlar: “kind” — mehribon, yaxshi qalbli; “friendly” — do‘stona, ochiq; “funny” — kulgili, odamlarni kuldiradigan; “clever” — aqlli; “hard-working” — mehnatkash; “polite” — xushmuomala, odobli. Bular tavsifnoma, rezyume va do‘st haqida gapirishda eng ko‘p ishlatiladigan so‘zlar.
scenes.say: My teacher is kind and polite. Sardor is funny and clever. My mum is very hard-working.
scenes.say_uz: O‘qituvchim mehribon va xushmuomala. Sardor kulgili va aqlli. Oyim juda mehnatkash.

scenes.title: Xarakter: boshqa sifatlar

examples.t: My sister is shy and quiet.

scenes.say_native: Yana bir guruh: “shy” — uyatchan, “quiet” — kamgap, jim. “Lazy” — dangasa, “rude” — qo‘pol, odobsiz. “Honest” — rostgo‘y, “generous” — saxiy, qo‘li ochiq, “serious” — jiddiy. E’tibor bering, “honest” so‘zida “h” harfi aytilmaydi: “ONest”. Shuning uchun “an honest man” deymiz. “Shy” yomon sifat emas, bu shunchaki odamning tabiati.
scenes.say: My sister is shy and quiet. My uncle is honest and generous. Our boss is very serious.
scenes.say_uz: Singlim uyatchan va kamgap. Amakim rostgo‘y va saxiy. Rahbarimiz juda jiddiy.

scenes.title: What's he like? va What does he look like?
board: What is she like? → xarakter (u qanday odam?)
What does she look like? → tashqi ko‘rinish
She's kind. / She's tall with dark hair.

examples.t: What's your boss like? — He's friendly.
What does she look like? — She's short with curly hair.
examples.uz: U qanaqa ko‘rinishda? — U past bo‘yli, sochi jingalak.

scenes.say_native: Ikki muhim savol. “What is she like?” — u qanday odam? Bu xarakter haqida savol, javob: “She’s kind and funny.” “What does she look like?” — u qanaqa ko‘rinishda? Bu tashqi ko‘rinish haqida, javob: “She’s tall with dark hair.” Bu yerda “like” — yoqtirmoq emas, “o‘xshash, qanday” degan ma’noni beradi. O‘zbekchada ikkalasi ham “u qanaqa?”
scenes.say: What's your new teacher like? She's very friendly. What does she look like? She's tall with short dark hair.
scenes.say_uz: Yangi o‘qituvchingiz qanday odam? U juda do‘stona. U qanaqa ko‘rinishda? U baland bo‘yli, qisqa qora sochli.

scenes.title: How is he? emas
board: ✗ How is your brother? (= tasvirlash uchun)
✗ What does she looks like? → ✓ What does she look like?
scenes.say_native: Xato: odamni tasvirlashni so‘rab “How is your brother?” deyish. “How is he?” — uning ahvoli qanday, sog‘ligi yaxshimi degan savol, javob: “He’s fine.” Tasvir uchun “What is he like?” kerak. Ikkinchi xato: “What does she looks like?” “Does” bor joyda fe’l “-s” olmaydi: “What does she look like?”
scenes.say: How is your brother? He's fine, thanks. What's your brother like? He's funny and clever.
scenes.say_uz: Akangizning ahvoli qanday? Yaxshi, rahmat. Akangiz qanday odam? U kulgili va aqlli.

scenes.title: Qaysi savol?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ekranda uchta javob bor. Siz har biri uchun savolni toping: “What is he like?”, “What does she look like?” yoki “How are you?” Birinchi javob: baland bo‘yli, sariq sochli. Ikkinchi javob: dangasa, lekin juda kulgili. Uchinchi javob: yaxshi, rahmat. Savollarni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Find the question. One: She's tall with blond hair. Two: He's lazy but very funny. Three: I'm fine, thanks.
scenes.say_uz: Savolni toping. Bir: U baland bo‘yli, sariq sochli. Ikki: U dangasa, lekin juda kulgili. Uch: Yaxshi, rahmat.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchisi tashqi ko‘rinish, demak savol: “What does she look like?” Ikkinchisi xarakter: “What is he like?” Uchinchisi hol-ahvol: “How are you?” Agar uchalasini ham to‘g‘ri topgan bo‘lsangiz, ajoyib. Bu savollar tanishuv va suhbatda juda ko‘p ishlatiladi.
scenes.say: What does she look like? What is he like? How are you?
scenes.say_uz: U qanaqa ko‘rinishda? U qanday odam? Qalaysiz?

scenes.title: Sifatning o‘rni
board: be + adjective: The man is tall.
a red car · The car is red.

examples.t: She has got a new phone.

scenes.say_native: Sifat gapda ikki joyda turadi. Birinchisi: otdan oldin. “A tall man” — baland bo‘yli erkak, “a red car” — qizil mashina. Ikkinchisi: “be” fe’lidan keyin. “The man is tall”, “The car is red.” Xushxabar: o‘zbek tilida ham sifat otdan oldin keladi: “qizil mashina”. Shuning uchun bu qoida siz uchun oson.
scenes.say: She has got a new phone. Her phone is new. It's a beautiful city. The city is beautiful.
scenes.say_uz: Uning yangi telefoni bor. Uning telefoni yangi. Bu chiroyli shahar. Shahar chiroyli.

scenes.title: Sifat o‘zgarmaydi
board: a tall boy → two tall boys
scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida sifat hech qachon o‘zgarmaydi. Birlikda ham, ko‘plikda ham, erkak uchun ham, ayol uchun ham bir xil: “a tall boy”, “two tall boys”, “a tall girl”. O‘zbek tilida ham shunday: “baland bola”, “baland bolalar”. Rus tilini bilsangiz, u yerda “высокий”, “высокая”, “высокие” deb o‘zgaradi. Ingliz tilida bunday moslashuv yo‘q.
scenes.say: A tall boy, two tall boys. An old house, three old houses. He is tall. They are tall.
scenes.say_uz: Baland bola, ikki baland bola. Eski uy, uchta eski uy. U baland. Ular baland.

scenes.title: a yoki an — sifatga qarab
board: a + undosh tovush: a big apple
an + unli tovush: an old car, an honest man
scenes.say_native: Muhim nozik joy. Otdan oldin sifat tursa, “a” yoki “an” sifatning birinchi tovushiga qarab tanlanadi. “An apple”, lekin “a big apple”, chunki “big” undosh bilan boshlanadi. “A car”, lekin “an old car”. “An honest man”, chunki “honest”dagi “h” aytilmaydi.
scenes.say: An apple. A big apple. A car. An old car. An honest man. An expensive bag.
scenes.say_uz: Olma. Katta olma. Mashina. Eski mashina. Rostgo‘y odam. Qimmat sumka.

scenes.title: Tartib va artikl xatolari
board: ✗ a car red → ✓ a red car
✗ two bigs houses → ✓ two big houses
✗ She is beautiful girl. → ✓ She is a beautiful girl.
✗ He is a tall. → ✓ He is tall.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta tipik xato. Bir: sifatni otdan keyin qo‘yish: “a car red” emas, “a red car”. Ikki: sifatga ko‘plik qo‘shish: “bigs houses” emas, “big houses”. Uch: artiklni tushirib qoldirish: “She is beautiful girl” emas, “She is a beautiful girl”. To‘rt: ot yo‘q bo‘lsa artikl qo‘shish: “He is a tall” emas, shunchaki “He is tall”.
scenes.say: A red car. Two big houses. She is a beautiful girl. He is tall.
scenes.say_uz: Qizil mashina. Ikkita katta uy. U chiroyli qiz. U baland bo‘yli.

scenes.title: Bir nechta sifat ketma-ket

examples.t: She has got a lovely small white cat.
examples.uz: Uning yoqimli kichkina oq mushugi bor.

scenes.say_native: Bir nechta sifat kelganda ingliz tilida ma’lum tartib bor. Avval fikr, baho: “nice”, “beautiful”, “lovely”. Keyin o‘lcham: “big”, “small”, “long”. Keyin yosh yoki eskilik: “old”, “new”, “young”. Oxirida rang: “red”, “black”. Masalan: “a beautiful old red car”, “long black hair”.
scenes.say: A nice big house. A beautiful old red car. A lovely small white cat. Long black hair.
scenes.say_uz: Yoqimli katta uy. Chiroyli eski qizil mashina. Yoqimli kichkina oq mushuk. Uzun qora soch.

scenes.title: Tartibga soling
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ekrandagi so‘zlarni to‘g‘ri tartibga soling. Esingizda bo‘lsin: avval baho, keyin o‘lcham, keyin yosh, oxirida rang va ot. Uchta birikmani baland ovozda ayting. Shoshilmang, har bir so‘zning vazifasini o‘ylang: qaysi biri baho, qaysi biri o‘lcham, qaysi biri rang. Artiklga ham e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Put the words in order. One: car, old, a, black. Two: hair, curly, long. Three: a, bag, small, nice, brown.
scenes.say_uz: So‘zlarni tartibga soling. Bir: mashina, eski, a, qora. Ikki: soch, jingalak, uzun. Uch: a, sumka, kichkina, yoqimli, jigarrang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchisi: “an old black car”. Diqqat qiling: “old” unli tovush bilan boshlangani uchun “a” emas, “an” bo‘ldi. Ikkinchisi: “long curly hair”, avval uzunlik, keyin shakl. Uchinchisi: “a nice small brown bag”, avval baho, keyin o‘lcham, keyin rang. Agar “an” ni payqagan bo‘lsangiz, siz juda diqqatli o‘quvchisiz.
scenes.say: An old black car. Long curly hair. A nice small brown bag.
scenes.say_uz: Eski qora mashina. Uzun jingalak soch. Yoqimli kichkina jigarrang sumka.

scenes.title: Very — juda
board: very tall · very kind · very cold
scenes.say_native: Sifatni kuchaytirish uchun “very” — juda, ishlatiladi. U doim sifatdan oldin turadi: “very tall”, “very kind”, “It’s very cold today.” Inkorda “not very” — unchalik … emas, degan ma’noni beradi: “He isn’t very tall” — u unchalik baland emas. Bu juda foydali, chunki salbiy narsani yumshoq aytishga yordam beradi.
scenes.say: It's very cold today. She is a very good teacher. The film isn't very interesting.
scenes.say_uz: Bugun juda sovuq. U juda yaxshi o‘qituvchi. Film unchalik qiziq emas.

scenes.title: Quite — ancha, anchagina
board: quite a + adjective + noun: quite a big house
scenes.say_native: “Quite” — ancha, anchagina, degan ma’noda. Britaniya ingliz tilida u “very” dan kuchsizroq: “not very” dan ko‘proq, “very” dan kamroq. “The test is quite easy” — test ancha oson, lekin juda oson emas. Diqqat: ot bilan ishlatganda tartib boshqacha: “quite a big house”, “a quite big house” emas.
scenes.say: The test is quite easy. My flat is quite small. It's quite a big house.
scenes.say_uz: Test ancha oson. Kvartiram ancha kichik. Bu anchagina katta uy.

scenes.title: Too — haddan tashqari
board: This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it.

examples.t: The shoes are too small for me.
It's very hot, but I like it.

scenes.say_native: “Too” — haddan tashqari, kerakdan ortiq. U doim muammoni bildiradi: “This coffee is too hot. I can’t drink it” — qahva haddan tashqari issiq, icholmayman. “The shoes are too small” — tuflilar kichik, kiyolmayman. “Very” esa shunchaki kuchaytiradi va muammo bo‘lishi shart emas: “It’s very hot, but I like it.”
scenes.say: This coffee is too hot. I can't drink it. These shoes are too small. I can't wear them.
scenes.say_uz: Bu qahva haddan tashqari issiq. Uni icholmayman. Bu tuflilar juda kichik. Ularni kiyolmayman.

scenes.title: O‘zbek tili bilan solishtirish

examples.t: The bag is too heavy. I can't carry it.

scenes.say_native: Nega o‘zbek o‘quvchilari “very” va “too” ni chalkashtiradi? Chunki o‘zbekchada ikkalasi ham ko‘pincha “juda” bilan aytiladi: “juda yaxshi” va “juda og‘ir, ko‘tarolmayman”. Ingliz tilida esa farq bor: maqtov yoki oddiy kuchaytirish — “very”, muammo yoki ortiqchalik — “too”.
scenes.say: Very good. Very nice. But: too heavy, too expensive, too late. And: I like tea. Me too!
scenes.say_uz: Juda yaxshi. Juda yoqimli. Lekin: haddan tashqari og‘ir, juda qimmat, juda kech. Va: Men choy yoqtiraman. Men ham!

scenes.title: Too beautiful — xato maqtov
board: ✗ He is very much tall. → ✓ He is very tall.
✗ a quite big house → ✓ quite a big house
scenes.say_native: Uchta xato. Birinchisi: maqtash uchun “too” ishlatish. “Your dress is too beautiful” desangiz, “ko‘ylagingiz haddan tashqari chiroyli, bu yomon” degandek eshitiladi. To‘g‘risi: “very beautiful”. Ikkinchisi: “very much tall”. Sifat oldida faqat “very” keladi. “Very much” fe’l bilan ishlatiladi: “I like it very much.”
scenes.say: Your dress is very beautiful! He is very tall. I like it very much. It's quite a big house.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘ylagingiz juda chiroyli! U juda baland bo‘yli. Bu menga juda yoqadi. Bu anchagina katta uy.

scenes.title: Very yoki too?
board: 1) The tea is ___ hot. I can't drink it.
3) I can't buy this car. It's ___ expensive.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. To‘rtta gapda bo‘sh joyga “very” yoki “too” qo‘ying. Har gapda o‘zingizga savol bering: bu yerda muammo bormi? Muammo bo‘lsa “too”, bo‘lmasa “very”. Gaplarni to‘liq baland ovozda o‘qing. Masalan, birinchi gapda ikkinchi qismga qarang: “I can’t drink it”. Bu sizga katta ishora.
scenes.say: Very or too? One: The tea is … hot. I can't drink it. Two: Your garden is … beautiful! Three: I can't buy this car. It's … expensive. Four: Thank you! You are … kind.
scenes.say_uz: Very yoki too? Bir: Choy … issiq. Uni icholmayman. Ikki: Bog‘ingiz … chiroyli! Uch: Bu mashinani sotib ololmayman. U … qimmat. To‘rt: Rahmat! Siz … mehribonsiz.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “too hot”, chunki icholmaymiz, bu muammo. Ikkinchi: “very beautiful”, bu maqtov. Uchinchi: “too expensive”, chunki sotib ololmaymiz. To‘rtinchi: “very kind”, bu minnatdorchilik. Ko‘rdingizmi, “can’t” so‘zi ko‘pincha “too” uchun yaxshi ishora bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: The tea is too hot. Your garden is very beautiful. It's too expensive. You are very kind.
scenes.say_uz: Choy haddan tashqari issiq. Bog‘ingiz juda chiroyli. U juda qimmat. Siz juda mehribonsiz.

scenes.title: Not very — muloyim usul
board: He is short. → He isn't very tall.
The film is bad. → It isn't very good.
She is unfriendly. → She isn't very friendly.
scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida so‘zlashuvchilar salbiy narsani ko‘pincha to‘g‘ridan to‘g‘ri aytmaydi. “The film is bad” o‘rniga “It isn’t very good” deyishadi. “He is short” o‘rniga “He isn’t very tall.” “She is rude” o‘rniga “She isn’t very polite.” Ma’no deyarli bir xil, lekin ohang ancha yumshoq.
scenes.say: The film isn't very good. My neighbour isn't very friendly. The hotel isn't very clean.
scenes.say_uz: Film unchalik yaxshi emas. Qo‘shnim unchalik do‘stona emas. Mehmonxona unchalik toza emas.

scenes.title: Qarama-qarshi sifatlar: ko‘rinish

examples.t: My hair is short, but my sister's hair is long.
examples.uz: Mening sochim qisqa, singlimniki esa uzun.

scenes.say_native: Sifatlarni juftlab o‘rgansangiz, ikki barobar tez yodlaysiz. “Tall” — “short”, bo‘y haqida. “Long” — “short”, uzunlik haqida. Demak “short” ikki ma’noli: past bo‘yli va qisqa. “Old” ham ikki juftli: odam uchun “young — old”, narsa uchun “new — old”.
scenes.say: Tall, short. Long, short. Young, old. New, old. Big, small.
scenes.say_uz: Baland, past. Uzun, qisqa. Yosh, keksa. Yangi, eski. Katta, kichik.

scenes.title: Qarama-qarshi sifatlar: xarakter

examples.t: She is hard-working, but her brother is lazy.

scenes.say_native: Xarakterda ko‘p sifatlarning qarama-qarshisi “un-” old qo‘shimchasi bilan yasaladi: “kind — unkind”, “friendly — unfriendly”, “happy — unhappy”. Bu o‘zbekchadagi “-siz” yoki “be-” ga o‘xshaydi: odobli — odobsiz, baxtli — baxtsiz. Lekin hamma so‘zga “un-” qo‘shilmaydi: “polite” ning juftini “impolite” yoki “rude”, “hard-working” niki “lazy”.
scenes.say: Kind, unkind. Friendly, unfriendly. Happy, unhappy. Polite, rude. Hard-working, lazy.
scenes.say_uz: Mehribon, mehrsiz. Do‘stona, do‘stona emas. Baxtli, baxtsiz. Xushmuomala, qo‘pol. Mehnatkash, dangasa.

scenes.title: Narsalarni tasvirlash

examples.t: The bag is light, not heavy.

scenes.say_native: Narsalar uchun eng kerakli juftlar: “cheap — expensive” — arzon va qimmat, “clean — dirty” — toza va iflos, “easy — difficult” — oson va qiyin, “heavy — light” — og‘ir va yengil, “hot — cold” — issiq va sovuq, “comfortable — uncomfortable” — qulay va noqulay. Do‘konda, mehmonxonada, uy ijarasida aynan shu so‘zlar kerak bo‘ladi. “Comfortable” so‘zi talaffuzda qisqaradi: “KUMF-tə-bəl”.
scenes.say: This chair is comfortable. The room is clean. The bag is light. The exam is difficult.
scenes.say_uz: Bu stul qulay. Xona toza. Sumka yengil. Imtihon qiyin.

scenes.title: Juftni to‘g‘ri tanlang
board: ✗ an old man ↔ a new man → ✓ a young man
✗ a light man (= yengil odam) → ✓ a slim man
scenes.say_native: Xatolar: “old” ning juftini kontekstga qarab tanlang. Odam uchun “young”, narsa uchun “new”. “A new man” deyilsa, “yangi kelgan odam” degan boshqa ma’no chiqadi. Ikkinchi: “unpolite” degan so‘z yo‘q, “impolite” yoki “rude” deyiladi. Uchinchi: “light” narsaning vazni uchun. Odamni “light” emas, “slim” yoki “thin” deb tasvirlaymiz.
scenes.say: An old man, a young man. An old car, a new car. Polite, impolite.
scenes.say_uz: Keksa odam, yosh odam. Eski mashina, yangi mashina. Xushmuomala, odobsiz.

scenes.title: Qarama-qarshisini ayting
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Beshta so‘z yoki birikma. Har birining qarama-qarshisini tez ayting. Uchinchisiga e’tibor bering: bu narsa, odam emas, demak juftni ehtiyotkorlik bilan tanlang. Artikl o‘zgaradimi yoki yo‘qmi, buni ham o‘ylab ko‘ring. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Say the opposite. Expensive. Friendly. An old phone. Hard-working. Heavy.
scenes.say_uz: Qarama-qarshisini ayting. Qimmat. Do‘stona. Eski telefon. Mehnatkash. Og‘ir.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “expensive” — “cheap”. “Friendly” — “unfriendly”. “An old phone” — “a new phone”, chunki telefon narsa, “young phone” bo‘lmaydi, va artikl ham “an” dan “a” ga o‘zgaradi. “Hard-working” — “lazy”. “Heavy” — “light”. To‘rt yoki besh to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, a’lo natija.
scenes.say: Cheap. Unfriendly. A new phone. Lazy. Light.
scenes.say_uz: Arzon. Do‘stona emas. Yangi telefon. Dangasa. Yengil.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: urg‘u
scenes.say_native: Talaffuz. Urg‘uga e’tibor bering: “FRIENDly”, “BEAUtiful”, “GENerous” — birinchi bo‘g‘inda. “PoLITE” va “inTELligent” da esa urg‘u boshqa joyda. “Handsome” so‘zida “d” aytilmaydi: “HANsəm”. Va eng muhimi: “quite” va “quiet” ni farqlang. “Quite” — bir bo‘g‘in, “kwayt”, ancha degani. “Quiet” — ikki bo‘g‘in, “KWAY-ət”, jim, kamgap degani.
scenes.say: Friendly. Beautiful. Generous. Polite. Intelligent. Handsome. Quite. Quiet. He is quite quiet.
scenes.say_uz: Do‘stona. Chiroyli. Saxiy. Xushmuomala. Aqlli. Kelishgan. Ancha. Kamgap. U ancha kamgap.

scenes.title: Takrorlang
scenes.say_native: Takrorlang. “A tall man” birikmasida “a” juda qisqa, kuchsiz “ə” bo‘lib aytiladi, alohida urg‘u olmaydi. “An honest man” da esa “an” va “honest” qo‘shilib ketadi: “ə-NO-nist”. Uchta gapni meni kuzatib baland ovozda takrorlang. Ritmga quloq soling: urg‘uli so‘zlar baland va aniq, kichik so‘zlar esa tez va yengil aytiladi.
scenes.say: A tall man. She's quite quiet. He's an honest man.
scenes.say_uz: Baland bo‘yli erkak. U ancha kamgap. U rostgo‘y odam.

scenes.title: O‘zingizni tekshiring
scenes.say_native: Tekshiring. “A” ni “ey” deb cho‘zib aytmadingizmi? Gap ichida u doim qisqa “ə”. “An honest” ni ikki bo‘lak qilib emas, bir oqimda aytdingizmi? “Quite quiet” da birinchi so‘z bir bo‘g‘in, ikkinchisi ikki bo‘g‘in bo‘lishi kerak. Agar qiyin bo‘lsa, sekin aytib, asta-sekin tezlashtiring. Ona tili egalari aynan shunday bog‘lab gapiradi.
scenes.say: A tall man. An honest man. Quite. Quiet.
scenes.say_uz: Baland bo‘yli erkak. Rostgo‘y odam. Ancha. Kamgap.

scenes.title: Tinglang: aeroportda kutib olish
board: Who is Kamol? What does he look like?
scenes.say_native: Endi dialogni tinglang. Lola do‘sti Jeykdan akasi Kamolni aeroportda kutib olishni so‘rayapti. Jeyk Kamolni hech qachon ko‘rmagan. Tinglab bo‘lgach, savollarga javob berasiz: Kamol qanday ko‘rinishda, sochi va ko‘zlari qanday, xarakteri qanday? Notanish so‘zlar bo‘lsa, xavotir olmang, asosiy ma’noni tushunishga harakat qiling.
scenes.say: Jake, can you meet my brother Kamol at the airport? Sure. What does he look like? He's tall and quite slim. He's got short black hair and brown eyes. And he's got glasses. OK. What's he like? He's very friendly, but he's a bit shy at first. Don't worry. I'm not very shy!
scenes.say_uz: Jeyk, akam Kamolni aeroportda kutib ololasanmi? Albatta. U qanaqa ko‘rinishda? U baland bo‘yli va ancha xipcha. Sochi qisqa qora, ko‘zlari jigarrang. Va ko‘zoynagi bor. Xo‘p. U qanday odam? U juda do‘stona, lekin boshida biroz uyatchan. Xavotir olma. Men unchalik uyatchan emasman!

scenes.title: Savollarga javob bering
scenes.say_native: Savollar. Kamol baland bo‘yli yoki past bo‘yli? Uning sochi qanday? Ko‘zlari qanday rangda? Xarakteri qanday? Javoblarni to‘liq gap bilan ayting, masalan: “He is …”, “He has got …”. Agar biror javobni eslay olmasangiz, keyingi qismda dialog matnini ekranda ko‘rasiz.
scenes.say: Is Kamol tall or short? What is his hair like? What colour are his eyes? What is he like?
scenes.say_uz: Kamol baland bo‘yli yoki past bo‘yli? Sochi qanday? Ko‘zlari qanday rangda? U qanday odam?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1) He is tall and quite slim.
2) He has got short black hair.
4) He is very friendly but a bit shy.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: Kamol baland bo‘yli va ancha xipcha. Uning sochi qisqa va qora. Ko‘zlari jigarrang, yana ko‘zoynak taqadi: “he’s got glasses”. Xarakteri: juda do‘stona, lekin boshida biroz uyatchan. Yangi ibora: “a bit” — biroz. U ko‘pincha salbiy sifatlar bilan ishlatiladi: “a bit shy”, “a bit lazy”.
scenes.say: He's tall and quite slim. He's got short black hair and brown eyes. He's very friendly but a bit shy.
scenes.say_uz: U baland bo‘yli va ancha xipcha. Sochi qisqa qora, ko‘zlari jigarrang. U juda do‘stona, lekin biroz uyatchan.

scenes.title: Tinglang: yangi kvartira
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Ikki dugona, Dilnoza va Emma, Dilnozaning yangi kvartirasi haqida gaplashyapti. Diqqat bilan tinglang: kvartira qanday, qimmatmi yoki arzonmi, oshxonada qanday muammo bor va qo‘shnilar qanday odamlar? “Very”, “quite”, “too” so‘zlariga alohida quloq soling.
scenes.say: So, what's your new flat like? It's lovely! It's quite big and very bright. Is it expensive? No, it isn't very expensive. Great! And the kitchen? Well, the kitchen is too small. I can't cook there with friends. Oh no! What are your neighbours like? They're old, but very kind and quiet.
scenes.say_uz: Xo‘sh, yangi kvartirang qanday? Ajoyib! U ancha katta va juda yorug‘. Qimmatmi? Yo‘q, unchalik qimmat emas. Zo‘r! Oshxona-chi? Hm, oshxona juda kichkina. U yerda do‘stlar bilan ovqat pishirolmayman. Voy! Qo‘shnilaring qanday odamlar? Ular keksa, lekin juda mehribon va tinch.

scenes.title: Savollarga javob bering
scenes.say_native: Savollar: kvartira kattami? Qimmatmi? Qanday muammo bor? Qo‘shnilar qanday odamlar? Javob berishda “very”, “quite”, “not very” va “too” so‘zlarini dialogdagidek aniq ishlating. Bitta so‘z farqi ma’noni o‘zgartiradi, shuning uchun juda diqqatli bo‘ling.
scenes.say: Is the flat big? Is it expensive? What is the problem? What are the neighbours like?
scenes.say_uz: Kvartira kattami? Qimmatmi? Muammo nima? Qo‘shnilar qanday odamlar?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1) It's quite big and very bright.
4) They're old but very kind and quiet.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Kvartira ancha katta va juda yorug‘. Unchalik qimmat emas. Muammo: oshxona haddan tashqari kichik, u yerda do‘stlar bilan ovqat pishirib bo‘lmaydi. Mana “too” ning aniq ma’nosi. Qo‘shnilar keksa, lekin juda mehribon va tinch. “Quiet” bu yerda “shovqin qilmaydigan” degani. “Bright” — yorug‘, xona uchun ajoyib maqtov.
scenes.say: It's quite big and very bright. It isn't very expensive. The kitchen is too small. The neighbours are very kind and quiet.
scenes.say_uz: U ancha katta va juda yorug‘. Unchalik qimmat emas. Oshxona juda kichik. Qo‘shnilar juda mehribon va tinch.

scenes.title: Tasvir rejasi
board: 1) name + age: My friend Aziz is 20.
2) appearance: He is … He has got …
3) character: He is very … quite … a bit …
4) your opinion: I like him because …
scenes.say_native: Odamni tasvirlashning oson rejasi. Birinchi: ism va yosh. Ikkinchi: tashqi ko‘rinish — bo‘y, gavda, soch, ko‘z. Uchinchi: xarakter — ikki-uchta sifat, “very”, “quite”, “a bit” bilan. To‘rtinchi: o‘z fikringiz, masalan “I like him because he is funny.” Bu reja og‘zaki nutqda ham, yozuvda ham, hatto imtihonda ham ishlaydi.
scenes.say: My friend Aziz is twenty. He is tall and slim. He has got short dark hair. He is very funny and quite clever, but a bit lazy. I like him because he is kind.
scenes.say_uz: Do‘stim Aziz yigirma yoshda. U baland bo‘yli va xipcha. Sochi qisqa va qora. U juda kulgili va ancha aqlli, lekin biroz dangasa. Men uni yoqtiraman, chunki u mehribon.

scenes.title: Endi siz gapiring
board: He / She is ___. He / She has got ___.
He / She is very ___ and quite ___.
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy og‘zaki topshiriq. Oilangizdagi bir kishini yoki do‘stingizni tanlang va reja asosida kamida oltita gap ayting: ism va yosh, bo‘y va gavda, soch va ko‘z, ikki-uchta xarakter sifati va nega uni yaxshi ko‘rishingiz. “Very”, “quite”, “a bit” ni ishlatishni unutmang. Pauza paytida baland ovozda gapiring.
scenes.say: Now describe a person you know. Talk about appearance and character. You have twenty seconds. Start!
scenes.say_uz: Endi o‘zingiz bilgan bir odamni tasvirlang. Tashqi ko‘rinish va xarakter haqida gapiring. Yigirma soniyangiz bor. Boshlang!

scenes.title: Namuna javob
board: My mother is 45. She is medium height.
She has got long dark hair and brown eyes.
She is very kind and quite serious.
I love her because she is generous.
scenes.say_native: Namuna: “My mother is forty-five. She is medium height and slim. She has got long dark hair and brown eyes. She is very kind and quite serious, but she is very funny at home. I love her because she is generous.”
scenes.say: My mother is forty-five. She is medium height and slim. She has got long dark hair and brown eyes. She is very kind and quite serious. I love her because she is generous.
scenes.say_uz: Oyim qirq besh yoshda. U o‘rta bo‘yli va xipcha. Uning uzun qora sochi va jigarrang ko‘zlari bor. U juda mehribon va ancha jiddiy. Men uni yaxshi ko‘raman, chunki u saxiy.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
board: tall, slim · long dark hair · kind, funny, shy
a tall man · The man is tall. · two tall men
not very < quite < very · too = muammo
tall ↔ short · old ↔ young / new · kind ↔ unkind
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Tashqi ko‘rinish uchun sifatlarni o‘rgandik: bo‘y, gavda, soch, ko‘z, yosh. Xarakter sifatlarini va “What is he like?” bilan “What does he look like?” farqini bildik. Sifat otdan oldin yoki “be” dan keyin turadi va hech qachon o‘zgarmaydi. “Very” — juda, “quite” — ancha, “too” — haddan tashqari, muammo.
scenes.say: Great work! Now you can describe people and things in English.
scenes.say_uz: Zo‘r ish! Endi ingliz tilida odamlar va narsalarni tasvirlay olasiz.

scenes.title: Uyga vazifa
board: very / quite / a bit · has got
scenes.say_native: Uyga vazifa. Bir do‘stingizning tashqi ko‘rinishi va xarakterini sakkizta gap bilan yozing: to‘rtta gap tashqi ko‘rinish haqida, to‘rtta gap xarakter haqida. Mezon: kamida bitta “very”, bitta “quite” yoki “a bit”, “has got” bilan soch yoki ko‘z, va “hairs”, “too beautiful” kabi xatolar yo‘q. Keyin matnni baland ovozda o‘qing.
scenes.say: See you next time. Bye!
scenes.say_uz: Keyingi darsda ko‘rishamiz. Xayr!

homework_uz: Bir do‘stingizning tashqi ko‘rinishi va xarakterini 8 ta gap bilan yozing: 4 ta gap tashqi ko‘rinish (bo‘y, gavda, soch, ko‘z), 4 ta gap xarakter haqida. Mezon: kamida bitta very, bitta quite yoki a bit, has got bilan soch yoki ko‘z; hairs, high (odam uchun) va maqtovda too kabi xatolar yo‘q. Matnni baland ovozda o‘qing.

quiz.q: Your friend is 1.95 m. He is very ___.
“What is your sister like?” — Choose the best answer.
quiz.why_uz: “What is she like?” — xarakter haqida savol.
Sifat otdan oldin keladi; “old” unli bilan boshlangani uchun “an”.

quiz.q: This bag is ___ heavy. I can't carry it.
What is the opposite of “an old man”?
